title: Only through Mind’s Perception
paragraphs: We talk about like-minded couple, or the son taking after the father or the daughter the mother. The comparison is called oppu which can only be felt intuitively. It does not lend itself to any understanding based on realities without.
Much like oppu, uru means a mind event caused by viewing something never seen before. This again is felt only through faculties within.

The word veruppu which commonly means hatred has another meaning listed in the dictionary, cerivu, which also means, abundance or modesty. Whatever might be the meaning, hatred could only be felt through the heart.
Chastity is also related to the heart. Chastity cannot manifest itself in a material form.
Both ēr (beauty) and eḻil (splendour) fall under the category of words which don’t lend themselves to be differentiated in concrete terms.

Nāṇ bridles the feelings. Maṭam is a characteristic of women. Nōy is a medical condition. Vēṭkai and nukarvu are the urges to get the object of desire, and quite like them, love, jealousy, modesty and wisdom can only be felt. Thus they fall under the category of abstract things.

> Likeness, awe and abundance, > Fidelity of the loved to the lover, growth and loveliness, > Delicacy, coyness and credulousness, > Affliction, longing and enjoyment > Are all terms of the abstract kind > Discernible to the mind’s eye; > They elude definitions of a concrete nature.
